newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate higher as players switch to dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate higher as players switch to dlrs.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates was up 30 basis points at 19.30 percent in early trade on Monday as some foreign investors switched to pesos to take advantage of a relatively cheap dollar, traders said.
Analysts said they nonetheless expected secondary market rates to level off if the peso were to slide.
"I would expect rates to stabilize and be under less pressure once the peso reaches a minimum level," a fixed-income analyst said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts had meanwhile weakened 1.3 centavos to 7.8675/7.8700 per dollar on demand for greenbacks.
Other analysts said macroeconomic indicators had paved the way for interest rates to fall in the near term despite the eraly rise in secondary rates.
"Inflation figures last week were good, as was the trade balance, and the peso is very solid, it just got a little too firm, that's all," another analyst said.
Overnight rates on bank paper had meanwhile risen 10 basis points to 19.50 percent.
Liquidity of 2.242 billion pesos was due to return to the system from prior central bank operations.
